s1.syndrome_frame: fever, hypotension, and rash in a patient with a history of chronic infection and recent immunotherapy
salient_findings: erythematous patches and thin plaques with telangiectases and hyperpigmentation
key_facts: patient is a woman in her 50s
history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis
treated with fluconazole
recently stopped pembrolizumab due to morbilliform reaction
new skin eruption appeared 1-2 weeks before admission
skin eruption is widespread and asymptomatic
laboratory tests show low white blood cell count, low hemoglobin, and low platelet count
blood culture results show no growth
serum tests for fungal and viral infections are negative
skin biopsy shows intravascular atypical cells

differentials: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified
Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma)
per_call: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified

Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma)

shortlist.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma (IVLBCL)
shortlist.why_kept: skin biopsy shows intravascular atypical cells, consistent with IVLBCL

shortlist.label: Intravascular NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type
shortlist.why_kept: skin biopsy shows intravascular atypical cells, and patient has history of immunotherapy

shortlist.label: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: patient presents with fever, hypotension, and rash, and has history of chronic infection

shortlist.label: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type
shortlist.why_kept: patient has history of immunotherapy and presents with widespread skin eruption

shortlist.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: patient presents with fever, hypotension, and rash, and has history of chronic infection and immunotherapy

raw.rationale: The presence of intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy and the patient's symptoms of fever, hypotension, and rash, along with laboratory findings of low white blood cell count, low hemoglobin, and low platelet count, are consistent with IVLBCL, a rare and aggressive form of lymphoma that often presents with systemic symptoms and skin involvement.

rejected.label: Intravascular NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type
rejected.why: While it is a possibility, the lack of specific nasal involvement and the presence of atypical cells on skin biopsy without clear NK/T-cell markers make it less likely.

rejected.label: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with skin lesions and leukemic dissemination, but the biopsy findings and clinical presentation do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not align with the typical nasal cavity involvement and NK/T-cell immunophenotype of this lymphoma.

rejected.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While it can present with systemic symptoms and skin involvement, the biopsy findings of intravascular atypical cells are not characteristic of this lymphoma.
